records.name: San Salvador Council 283, Knights of Columbus
records.summary: A Catholic fraternal service club in South Philadelphia that runs food, coat and blood drives and takes part in parish Masses and festivals.
records.what_you_do: Help with the council's food and coat collections, give blood at a drive, or come to a public Mass, parade or festival. Membership is a separate path that starts with the site's contact form.

schedule.text: No regular meeting night is posted. Drives, Masses and festivals are listed by date. The next listed event is the Columbus Day Mass, parade and festival on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026.

cost.text: Event fees are not listed, and membership dues are not published on the site.

first_step.how: Go to the Columbus Day Mass, parade and festival on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, or use the Join the Knights page on kofc283philly.org to ask about membership.
first_step.basis: The public events are open to anyone and the site has a clear way to ask about joining, but membership rules are not published.

records.notes: The batch name was Knights of Columbus, Council. The site calls the council San Salvador Council 283. The meeting address, email and phone are not published, so no location is recorded. The Sept. 25, 2026 blood drive and the August 2026 Mass are already past. Social media accounts are linked on the site, but their URLs were not recorded. Membership requirements are not stated on the site.

records.name: The Lady Hoofers Tap Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia tap nonprofit that creates its own tap work, teaches classes and runs a youth ensemble. It stages a yearly holiday show.
records.what_you_do: Take a class in the Class Series, join the Youth Ensemble, or see The Tapcracker holiday show. The group also does performance and education outreach in the community.

schedule.text: The Tapcracker holiday show, now in its 10th year: Saturday, Dec. 12, 2026 at 11 am, 3 pm and 7:30 pm, and Sunday, Dec. 13, 2026 at 3 pm. Class and ensemble times are not posted on the site.

cost.text: Tapcracker tickets are $35 to $65 on the group's site. Class prices are not published.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for The Tapcracker on Dec. 12 or 13, 2026, or use the Email Us page on ladyhoofers.org to ask about the Class Series.
first_step.basis: Classes and a youth ensemble exist, but the site does not explain how to join, audition or pay for classes.

records.notes: The Cultural Fund calendar lists Tapcracker admission as free. The group's own page lists paid tickets at $35 to $65, so this record follows the group's page. The calendar entry should be checked. The site says the group focuses on women in tap, but it does not limit who may attend. No public email is shown (the contact link is obfuscated), so none is recorded. Ticket sales run through a separate ticket seller.

records.name: LandHealth Institute
records.summary: A West Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches people about nature at outdoor sites, works to revive neglected land and runs a native plant nursery. Volunteers can sign up through the website.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer, join as a member, or come to public events such as the free kayaking day at the Dragon Boat Dock in West Fairmount Park.

schedule.text: Events are posted by date on the group's site. The May 9, 2026 free kayaking day ran 1:30 to 5:30 pm, and the group called it the start of its 2026 kayaking season. No other dated program was found.

locations.label: Dragon Boat Dock, West Fairmount Park (2026 kayaking day)

cost.text: The May 2026 kayaking day was free, with no tickets on sale. Costs for other programs are not listed.

first_step.how: Sign up through the Become a Volunteer page on landhealthinstitute.org, or email info@landhealthinstitute.org to ask about the next volunteer day.
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up and events are open to the public with a posted way to start, and the kayaking day was open to all ages and skill levels.

records.notes: The homepage shows a copyright year but no dated news. Its newest dated item is the May 9, 2026 kayaking day, which the Love Your Park page lists as hosted by the group. The Love Your Park page is run by Fairmount Park Conservancy and Philadelphia Parks and Recreation. The site spells the name LandHealth Institute. The mailing address is a P.O. box and is not recorded. The nursery address is the visiting address the homepage gives.

records.name: Mayo Association of Philadelphia
records.summary: An Irish heritage association named as a Dougherty Award winner on the St. Patrick's Day Parade website. Its own page was not found, so its activities are not yet known.

first_step.how: Email the St. Patrick's Day Observance Association, the parade organizer, at info@phillyparade.com and ask how to reach the Mayo Association. That address belongs to the parade office, not the club.
first_step.basis: The parade office is the only public contact found for this club.

records.notes: The only public mention found is the parade site, which covers the 2026 parade but does not date this award. Status is probably_active on that basis, not confirmed. No website or contact for the club itself was found. The search budget ran out before this seed could be searched. Meetings, membership and location are not verified. Heritage tags are based on the name and the parade listing; the audience is not set.

records.name: Philadelphia GAA (Gaelic Athletic Association)
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Gaelic Athletic Association. Its site covers Gaelic football, hurling and camogie, and it has a youth page for young players.
records.what_you_do: Play on a Gaelic football, hurling or camogie team, join the youth program, or ask the group how to try the sport. Team and youth details sit on the group's Teams and Youth GAA pages.

locations.label: Limerick Field Complex, Pottstown, PA (a field the group lists; the Pottstown location comes from a public search result, not the group's site)

cost.text: No fees are published on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page on philadelphiagaa.com, or message the group through its Facebook or Instagram accounts, to ask about a trial session or the youth program.
first_step.basis: The site has team and youth pages, but no trial, learn-to-play or sign-up details appear in the text that could be read, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The seed said Players, but the group's site names itself the Philadelphia chapter of the GAA. The site shows no dated news, and its footer reads 2025, which is not evidence on its own, so status is probably_active. A parade site lists Philadelphia GAA as a likely award winner, undated. Other clubs found in search results: Glenside Gaelic Club is a youth club for ages 5 to 17 in the Glenside area, which is outside the city. It is not recorded here and is a candidate for future research.

records.name: Philadelphia Grotto
records.summary: A caving club founded in 1947 as a chapter of the National Speleological Society. Members explore caves, work to protect them and learn the sport together.
records.what_you_do: Come to a first-Thursday meeting to pick up a membership form. Members get trip information and a newsletter, and they vote in officer elections.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the first Thursday of the month, 7:30 to 9:30 pm, according to the meeting page. The page names an October 1 meeting without a year.

locations.label: Meets at a member's home in Media, PA (Delaware County). The location or video link is posted on the homepage.

cost.text: Membership is $12 a year for an individual or $18 for a family. Trip costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Check the homepage for the location or video link, then attend the next first-Thursday meeting at 7:30 pm to get a membership form.
first_step.basis: The group tells prospective members to attend a meeting to get a membership form, and it gives beginners safety advice about caving with experienced leaders.

records.notes: The group's old WordPress address redirects to phillygrotto.org. The meeting page names an October 1 meeting with no year. October 1 is a Thursday in 2026, so it may be this year's meeting, but the year is not printed. That is why the status is probably_active and no last sign of life is recorded. Meetings are held at a private home, so the street address is left out. The group is named for Philadelphia, but its meetings are in Delaware County, just outside the city. A reviewer should decide whether that counts as serving Philadelphia. No email is published; the About page mentions an email for the membership chair, but the address is not shown.

records.name: The Philadelphia Suns
records.summary: The seed list names a lion dance group in Philadelphia. No group page was found, so nothing is known yet about its practices or performances.

This seed was not searched online because the search budget ran out, so the record may be wrong. A reviewer should check it or drop it. Lion dance is filed under cultural dance as the closest tag.

records.name: Practice Yoga Co-op
records.summary: A worker-owned yoga co-op in Philadelphia where the teachers run classes, events and workshops together. Drop-in classes are by donation, and mats and props are free to use.
records.what_you_do: Drop in to a class without signing up and pay what you choose, with a suggested minimum of $15. Mats and props are free. The Iyengar classes taught by Ellen are priced separately, and the site does not give that price.

schedule.text: Drop-in classes run on the schedule posted on the site. The newest dated item is the Align and flow class with Mary on Oct. 14, 2026. Zoom classes with Ellen are listed on a separate site, practiceyogastudio.com.

locations.label: Studio, per a 2024 Philly Mag listing (not on the group's own site)

cost.text: Drop-in classes run on a donation with a suggested minimum of $15, and no one is turned away for lack of funds. Mats and props are free. The Iyengar class price is not listed.

first_step.how: Show up for a drop-in class without registering in advance, such as the Oct. 14, 2026 Align and flow class with Mary, and pay what you choose, with a suggested $15 minimum.
first_step.basis: Drop-ins need no advance sign-up and mats are free, but the site does not say beginner classes are offered.

records.notes: IDENTITY NOT CONFIRMED. The seed was Queen Village Yoga Co-op, taken from a Nextdoor page, and no page uses that exact name. The closest match is Practice Yoga Co-op, which a 2024 Philly Mag listing places at 804 S 4th St in Queen Village. The co-op's own site does not mention Queen Village and gives no street address. A reviewer should confirm it is the same co-op before publishing. Prices come from the co-op's own site: the site says a $15 suggested minimum, while the 2024 listing said $5. Ellen's Zoom and Iyengar classes are on practiceyogastudio.com, which was not read. The co-op is a worker-owned studio, not a nonprofit.

records.name: Bachelors Barge Club
records.summary: An adult rowing club on Boathouse Row. It teaches new rowers in one-person boats and coaches experienced rowers, but membership needs an application and approval.
records.what_you_do: Apply for membership, and take private lessons if you are new to rowing. Rowers move from one-person boats to team boats as they log miles on the river. Coaching is available to experienced rowers.

schedule.text: The club does not post a weekly schedule. Rowing and lessons run on the river, and no dated program was found on its pages.

cost.text: Adult dues are $650 a year for members 23 and over. Youth members aged 18 to 22 pay $380, or $225 for a summer-only rate. A student rate of $380 and family rates are also listed. The pricing page is undated.

first_step.how: Fill out the application form on the membership page at bachelorsbargeclub.org/membership/, or email the club to ask about private lessons for new rowers.
first_step.basis: New rowers are welcome, with private lessons and a handbook, but membership needs an application, approval and possibly a waiting list.

records.notes: The home page has placeholder text: a sample street address, a sample phone number and a sample email. So the club's own contact details may be out of date. The email on its pages is a Drexel University address. It is recorded as published, but it may be an old inbox, so confirm before relying on it. No dated news was found. The Schuylkill Navy directory lists the club as a full member. The street address is not recorded because the site's address is a placeholder. The club is on Boathouse Row.

records.name: College Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club at Boathouse Row for past and present University of Pennsylvania rowers. Membership is not open to the public.
records.notes: Hidden as out of scope because there is no public way in. Membership is limited to past and present University of Pennsylvania rowers, and alumni qualify only if they were varsity rowers. The rule comes from the Wikipedia article, which cites a 2009 regatta program whose link is dead. The club is at #11 Boathouse Row and is listed on the Schuylkill Navy directory. The group's own site was not found. The university athletics rowing page (pennathletics.com/rowing) is a team page and not a way for the public to join.

records.name: Conshohocken Rowing Center
records.summary: A rowing club in the borough of Conshohocken, outside Philadelphia. Its programs are for Conshohocken residents and for nearby school rowing programs.
records.notes: Out of area: the club meets in Conshohocken, not Philadelphia, and its programs serve Conshohocken residents and the school sculling centers it hosts. It is an associate member of the Schuylkill Navy. The site has no dated news, so status is only probably_active. Its email and mailing address are not recorded.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A member-run rowing club on Boathouse Row, organized in 1867. It runs summer sculling programs for young rowers and takes adult members who have two sponsors.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the summer Novice program, which is for young people who have never rowed, or apply for adult membership with two member sponsors. The club also runs racing programs for junior and U23 rowers.

schedule.text: Summer youth sculling programs on the Schuylkill River. The Novice program usually runs Monday to Thursday, 8 to 11 am. The newest dated item is a May 2025 post about the 2025 summer programs. No 2026 dates were found on the pages read.

cost.text: Adult member dues are $550 a year. Each summer youth program costs $800, separate from dues. Racing uniforms are not included in the Sculling Development or Junior fees.

first_step.how: Email board@crescentboatclub.org to ask about the summer Novice program, or submit the membership inquiry form at crescentboatclub.org/membership/ to ask about adult membership.
first_step.basis: A youth program takes people who have never rowed, but adult membership needs $550 a year in dues and two member sponsors.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a May 16, 2025 news post, so status is probably_active, not active. The Calendar of Events page was linked but not read, and it may list 2026 dates. Adult membership requires being over 21 and two member sponsors. Student membership covers people under 21, or under 23 if still in school. The Membership page's Pricing link was not read, so any fee changes after 2025 are not reflected.

records.name: Fairmount Rowing Association
records.summary: A rowing club at Boathouse Row #2, founded in 1877. It runs a summer program for junior rowers aged 17 and 19 and a masters program for adults.
records.what_you_do: Junior rowers join the summer program in sculling or sweep rowing, which ends with local regattas and possible trips to the Royal Canadian Henley for selected rowers. Adults can join the masters sculling or sweep program.

schedule.text: The 2026 summer junior program had an information meeting on June 16 and a parents meeting on June 17, both at 7 pm at the Temple Boathouse. Sessions ran 7 to 9 am from June 18 into late July. 2027 dates were not posted on the pages read.

cost.text: The junior page lists no program fees. The membership page still shows 2017 to 2018 dues, so current dues were not found.

first_step.how: Read the junior rowing page at fairmountrowing.org/junior-rowing-program, then ask the coach through the contact on that page about the next season's information meeting. The 2026 meeting was June 16.
first_step.basis: The junior program needs an application before an information meeting, and the adult dues shown are out of date, so the way in is not clear for adults.

records.notes: The membership page still shows dues for March 2017 to February 2018, so current adult dues were not found and none are recorded. Its contact there is a named individual, which is not recorded. Junior program fees were not published. The 2026 program information is a Google Drive document that was not read. The 2026 junior dates come from the junior page, which shows no publish date.

leads_only.name: Na Toraidhe Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Hurling and camogie club found in a search result. Its only page is a Zeffy donation page with no own website. That page lists an adult Learn to Hurl program in Roxborough (Sept. 3 to Oct. 15, 2026). Not recorded from a group site; left for future research.

notes: Batch had 15 seeds, all hand-picked seeds rather than park Friends groups, so the Friends-group contact rule did not apply. Verdicts: 13 publish, 1 hide, 1 out_of_area. Searches: 3 of 3 used (College Boat Club, Queen Village Yoga Co-op, Philadelphia GAA); the Suns, Scuba, O'Mahoney and Mayo seeds were not searched because the budget went to the seeds with real websites to find. Key flags for review: (1) Queen Village Yoga Co-op matched to Practice Yoga Co-op, identity not confirmed; (2) The Lady Hoofers Cultural Fund listing says free, but the group's own page shows paid Tapcracker tickets, so the group's page was used; (3) Philadelphia Grotto meets in Media (Delaware County), so its in-city status needs a call; the private meeting address is omitted; (4) Bachelors Barge Club's site has placeholder contact details; (5) Fairmount's membership page shows 2017 to 2018 dues, so no current adult dues are recorded. The Schuylkill Navy directory also names 12 other clubs outside this batch (Gillin, Malta, Pennsylvania Barge, Penn Athletic, Philadelphia Girls Rowing, Undine, University Barge, Vesper, Hines, Philadelphia City Rowing, Sedgeley, Whitemarsh Boat Club, and the Pennsylvania Center for Adaptive Sport). They were not checked and are dropped from this run for that reason; they are candidates for a later batch.
